::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 10th 1893  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MS Acland d.175.ff 178-9
:::

My dear [Miss Acland](people/person_8.qmd)
I am sending Pompei (it does not look natural) to [Christabel Coleridge](people/person_329.qmd) at Cheyne, Torquay, and it will be more convenient for her to let you know about it, as I am not the sole dictator of [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) now, but one of a triumvirate - being really, I suppose, rather dropped behind the present world.[^1]

I fear that any how the diagrams cannot be brought in, but that [the publisher](people/person_744.qmd) must decide, and they <u>may</u> think it long and minute

A ridiculous fabulous history of me declared that I never permitted a Roman Catholic to write in the packet, which was very untrue[.] I once had [Kathleen O’Meara](people/person_1096.qmd) and dropped her, not for her opinions, but for making the cannon fire a salute when William the Conqueror started for England, which destroyed my confidence in her [‘Old Castles’](other_books/otherbook_673.qmd).

I saw [Mrs Cooke Trench](people/person_367.qmd) last week. The party have not started yet as [Beatrice](people/person_655.qmd) feels bound to wait for young [Mr Compton](people/person_2118.qmd)’s coming of age ball. [Lady Heathcote](people/person_665.qmd) was then very unwell but was much better when last I heard [Helena](people/person_663.qmd) was not well but not seriously, and I expect to meet her at some of the [GFS](organizations/other_23.qmd) affairs next week

Yours very sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The article does not seem to have been published.
